text:
jordan.sre: seeing a spike in 503s for hosted inference in us-west starting ~15:21 UTC. alerting SRE. :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Pager sent to @jordan.sre and @ryan-eng-runtime (incident: INC-20260316-4289)
maria-support: customer ticket #4289 reporting timeouts + 503s, sample req ids: req_7a1, req_9f3. Happening on model=gpt-large-v2 only so far.
ryan-eng-runtime: I can see repeated runner exits in the logs. mix of SIGSEGV (exit code 139) and occasional OOM kills (exit code 137).
eli-mlops: we pushed a quantization profile to gpt-large-v2 earlier today at 15:12 UTC — might be related.
jordan.sre: impact: 5–7% 503 rate across the pool, customer-facing latency spikes. Routing fallback kicked in for some customers.
maria-support: customer is asking for repro steps and ETA.
ryan-eng-runtime: adding relevant log extract:
```
[2026-03-16T15:20:59Z] runner(pid=2145) ERROR: segfault at 0x7ffd3c2f kernel/attn.c:1045
[2026-03-16T15:21:00Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2145 (runner) total-vm:1234567kB, anon-rss:987654kB
[2026-03-16T15:21:01Z] containerd: container exited with code 139
```
ryan-eng-runtime: reproduction pattern: high QPS with long context windows + batch_size 32 + kv_prefetch enabled causes memory surge on some GPUs. Seen on p4d instances.
eli-mlops: I can revert the quantization profile immediately if we think it's correlated. Also can we try disabling kv_prefetch for that model as a quick test?
jordan.sre: yes please revert as a quick mitigation and disable kv_prefetch for the model route. Also start rolling restarts of the affected runner pool to clear bad processes.
oncall-bot: actioned: rollback quantization -> PR merged (r/1234), kv_prefetch flag set to false for gpt-large-v2 in route config.
ryan-eng-runtime: started a targeted restart of the us-west-hosted pool. Deploy-bot shows: rollout start -> 6 nodes -> sequential.
deploy-bot: Rollout update: 3/6 restarted, 0/6 failed.
maria-support: updated the customer with mitigations and asked if they'd accept temporary traffic routed to gpt-large-v1. They agreed.
eli-mlops: enabling fallback routing to gpt-large-v1 for affected customers now. Policy applied.
jordan.sre: immediate mitigation reduced 503s back to ~0.5% within 4 mins after restarts + rollback. Good.
ryan-eng-runtime: next steps: collect coredumps + GPU driver logs from affected hosts. Please enable ulimit cores on the pool and upload to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-4289/.
eli-mlops: I'll patch the runtime to cap kv_prefetch memory usage to 1GB and add a memory guardrail for future quantization profiles (PR r/1235).
jordan.sre: assign follow-up tasks: 1) postmortem (owner: jordan.sre) 2) regression test for quantized models (owner: eli-mlops) 3) autoscaler tuning to avoid overcommit (owner: ryan-eng-runtime).
maria-support: customer asked about SLA credit process; I created ticket internal: BILL-4289 and looped finance.
ryan-eng-runtime: quick repro command (dev-only) — please don't run against prod endpoints:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-v2","input":"<~3k tokens prompt>","max_tokens":1500,"batch_size":32}' &
done
```
jordan.sre: we should also add alerting for segfault rate per pool (not just 5xx rate). I'll add a ticket to infra alerting.
eli-mlops: uploading coredump index and analysis notes to the incident doc now. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4289 (internal).
maria-support: thanks all — I'll keep the customer posted and confirm SLA next steps after postmortem.
jordan.sre: thanks team. postmortem timeline: draft due EOD tomorrow. tagging: @ryan-eng-runtime @eli-mlops for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
